lede: A crude oil spike above $100/barrel tied to Strait of Hormuz tensions rippled through regional asset prices: Pakistan's stock exchange extended losses for a third session and the government imposed a fourth consecutive fuel-price hike, while the Philippine peso weakened to P62.535/dollar and the PSEi retreated. Separately, the IMF confirmed a mission to Islamabad on September 23 for the biannual review of Pakistan's $7 billion Extended Fund Facility.

countries.summary: The IMF said a mission will visit September 23 for the biannual review of the $7 billion Extended Fund Facility. The PSX fell for a third straight session amid Hormuz-linked oil price gains and political uncertainty, having already retreated below 174,000 on profit-taking earlier in the week; the rupee held nearly flat at 277.35/dollar. The government raised petrol Rs3.05 and diesel Rs5.37 per liter effective September 11 — the fourth consecutive increase, taking petrol to Rs370.80/liter — reflecting global crude pass-through. Islamabad also invited Belt and Road partners into CPEC Phase II, and SECP proposed reforms to expand the REIT sector.

Bankers and an industry report said non-performing loans have reached a record Tk 6.06 lakh crore, attributing the buildup to political patronage and impunity for wilful defaulters. Parliament passed a Bank Resolution (Amendment) Bill on September 9, and the central bank ordered disciplinary action against 13 Bangladesh Commerce Bank officials over Tk 4 crore in incentive-related irregularities. Prime Bank joined Bangladesh Bank's Tk 3,000 crore export-diversification refinance scheme. Separately, London's High Court froze roughly $250 million (£185 million) in UK property belonging to a former land minister under a National Crime Agency bankruptcy petition.

No substantive economic or financial reporting today. Coverage centered on security (TTP and Baloch militant attacks spreading into Pakistan's Balochistan) and humanitarian conditions (the UN warning of a deepening crisis and a REACH report citing 3.1 million internally displaced), alongside diplomatic meetings on trade with Bangladesh, Turkey, and Iran that produced no new figures or agreements.

Two weeks after Himalayan floods that killed more than 1,410 people with 5,651 still missing, coverage turned to the economic toll: The Diplomat reported that destruction of the Trishuli-Bhotekoshi trade corridor has caused economic collapse in Nepal's border region, and the foreign minister renewed a call for $20 million in climate compensation from major emitters. A September 9 New York Times report said USAID funding cuts have hampered flood relief efforts.

Royal Securities Exchange trading value rose 32% in August even as the number of trades and investors fell. The finance ministry introduced a new framework (September 8) to strengthen oversight of sovereign guarantees and on-lending.

The central bank's net foreign-currency position narrowed in August as liabilities outpaced asset growth, a reserve-adequacy signal. A new regulation targets 168 stalled tourism developments to recover $537 million owed to the state, and the tax authority (MIRA) said it recovered $32.2 million in unpaid state revenue. Bank of Maldives will discontinue overseas ATM cross-border fees, and officials said tourism is recovering from earlier Middle East conflict-related disruption.

Central-bank FDI data drew conflicting characterizations: BusinessWorld reported net inflows jumped 35% y/y in June even as they hit a two-month low, while the Inquirer described first-half FDI as 'losing momentum' amid growth concerns. BofA warned Philippine GDP growth may lag Southeast Asian peers this year on weak domestic demand, and BSP Governor Remolona earned a third consecutive 'A-' from Global Finance's central banker report card. The peso weakened 2.2 centavos to P62.535/dollar and the PSEi slipped as oil breached $100/barrel. Del Monte Pacific opened creditor talks to restructure amid liquidity pressure, and Moody's said DigiPlus has room for more debt after a first-time B1 rating.
